reason: 'visible' only means it can be seen. 'Conspicuous' means it stands out. 'Not visible' would wrongly become 'not conspicuous'.
'Divergent' (branches, lobes, sepals) means spreading apart.
'Eglandular' means no glands. The gland class is PO_0005656 (portion of secretory tissue, synonym gland).
'Unarmed' means no spines, thorns or prickles, so 'not spiny' fits.
'Parallel' on a leaf, vein or nerve means parallel venation. The constraint is already limited to these parts.
A 'naked' stem, scape or culm has no leaves. The constraint keeps out 'naked' meaning glabrous.
'Caudate-acuminate' means an acuminate apex drawn out into a tail. Caudate is the closest class.
'Acutish' means somewhat acute, which is subacute.
'Sheathed' on petiole, leaf base, bract or stipule means sheathing.
'Gland-tipped' means the part bears a gland at its tip.
'Broadened' means increased width.
'Armed' means bearing spines, thorns or prickles.
'Glandless' means no glands.
'Confluent' means running together or merging (veins, glands, spots). It does not mean fused organs (connate).
'Delicate' in floras usually means slender or fine. It does not mean fragile, and no better target exists.
'Reticulate-veined' means reticulate venation. The bearer is the leaf rather than the veins, which is a minor loss.
'Castaneous' means chestnut-coloured.
'Septate' means divided by septa (partitions). 'Split' means cleft, which is a different meaning.
'Hirsutulous' means minutely or slightly hirsute. The loss of 'slightly' is small.
'Eciliate' means without cilia.
A 'bulging' part projects out, which is prominent.
'Obtuse-rounded' is an obtuse apex that is rounded. Obtuse has the synonym roundish.
A dichasium is a cyme. 'Dichasial' describes a cymose inflorescence.
'Rolled' (margins revolute or involute, leaves convolute) is a specific rolling. 'Curled' is a different shape.
'Glomerulate' means clustered in small dense heads, which is aggregated.
'Semiterete' means half-round, flat on one side, which is plano-convex.
A broadly acute apex is still acute in the botanical sense. Only the angle detail is lost.
'Withered' means dried up and shrunken, which is shriveled.
Direct negation of thickened (increased thickness).
'Flaccid' means limp and soft. Flexible is the closest existing class.
'Semi-amplexicaul' means half-clasping the stem. Clasping is the closest class.
'Rooting' means rooting at the nodes of stems, so the shoot-borne root only fits on these parts. Elsewhere it is ambiguous.
'Vaginate' means sheathing.
'Chestnut brown' is a synonym of chestnut colour.
'Excentric' means off-centre, so 'not centered' fits.
'Semiglobose' means half-globose, which is hemispheroid.
'Lignified' means woody.
'Depressed globose' is a flattened sphere, which is oblate.
Elliptic has the synonym ellipsoid. 'Broadly' is lost.
A 'high' crest, wing, keel or ridge is one with increased height. The constraint is appropriate.
'Lingulate' means tongue-shaped, which is strap-shaped.
'Short-lived' means decreased life span.
'Capsular' means the fruit is a capsule.
'Apparent' means visible or evident. It does not mean conspicuous, as with 'visible' in R0001.
Direct negation of prominent.
With the constraint, 'separated' (internodes, whorls, spikelets) means distant.
'Mat' is dull only in French or as 'matt'. In English, 'mat' is a noun for a mat-forming habit. Limit it to surfaces.
'Chestnut' means chestnut colour.
A triangular-lanceolate shape is the same compound shape as lanceolate-triangular. Only the word order differs.
'Empty' glumes, lemmas and florets lack a fertile flower, which is sterile.
